1.explanation:
1. Dropdown/Dropdown.mdx & Dropdown/docs/overview.mdx — These two files describe the current API, markup and CSS tokens for the standard Dropdown component, which is the target of the change.  
2. FluidDropdown/FluidDropdown.mdx & FluidDropdown/docs/overview.mdx — The fluid variant shows how read-only is handled in a similar input component. Use it as a pattern for prop naming, style overrides, and story integration.  
3. Select/Select.mdx & Select/docs/overview.mdx — The Select component shares many behaviors and styling rules with Dropdown. Reviewing its implementation and docs helps ensure consistency in prop names, classNames, and token usage when adding the new read-only state.
1.bug_scenario:
The bug report calls out that the Dropdown component in our React package must support a new read-only variant. The two provided screenshots are design specifications showing:  
• The overall structure and spacing of the read-only dropdown (padding, border weights, icon placement), including default, small, default, large sizes and error state.  
• The color and typography tokens to apply in “no input” versus “filled” states (placeholder vs. primary text color, helper text color, disabled icon, border color).  

In essence, the dropdown must render visually like the enabled version (same layout and element positions) but not allow interactions when read-only, and adopt the proper styling for that state across all sizes and states (error, filled, empty). We also need to expose a readOnly prop, integrate it into the Playground story, and add RTL tests ensuring the read-only class is applied.
